title: Loops: `for`, `for range`, walking maps and strings

videos.script: Lesson 16 built types out of other types. This one repeats things. Go has exactly one loop, and its keyword is for. {{forms}} It comes in three shapes. One counts, one waits for a condition, and one runs until you stop it. There is no while, and you will see what the compiler makes of one. {{range}} Then range, which walks a collection for you. It hands you an index and a value. The value is a copy, and changing it changes nothing. You will watch a whole team keep its old scores. {{map}} Maps come next. Lesson 14 showed they have no order, so here you walk one safely, and remove entries as you go. {{string}} Last, strings. Ranging over a string does not give you bytes. It gives you runes, and where each one starts. A broken byte comes out as a replacement character, not as an error. By the end you can pick the right loop for a job, and say what each variable holds on every pass.
